title: Attachment
summary: A named point (with orientation) on a part: used by particles, beams, sounds, constraints, and animations to say 'right here'. Zero visual presence — pure positional marker.

properties.name: Position
properties.description: Offset from the parent part's center (in the part's local space).

properties.name: Orientation / Rotation
properties.description: Local rotation of the attachment's axes.

properties.name: Axis / SecondaryAxis
properties.description: Direction vectors used by constraints like HingeConstraint.

details.heading: Who uses attachments
details.body: ParticleEmitters and Sounds placed at the attachment emit from it; Beams and Ropes connect Attachment0/Attachment1; constraints (Hinge, VectorForce, Motor6D's C0/C1 logic) reference attachments; animation rigs are built from them.

explanation.whatItIs: A pushpin you stick into a part at an exact spot and angle. Effects, sounds, ropes, and motors then plug into that pin instead of fiddling with raw coordinates.
explanation.whyItExists: 'The muzzle of this gun', 'the top of this flagpole', 'the left wheel hub' — named local points beat magic-number offsets everywhere.
whenToUse: Particle emitter / sound placement (parent the emitter to the attachment)
whenNotToUse: For one-off world positions — just use a Vector3
As a visual marker — attachments render nothing
tips: Attachments move WITH their part — ideal for effects on moving objects
Name them clearly ('Muzzle', 'ExhaustL') — they show up in the Explorer
Use WorldCFrame to get the attachment's live world pose
commonMistakes: Parenting a ParticleEmitter to the part instead of the attachment and losing the offset
Forgetting constraints need matching attachments on BOTH parts

examples.title: Muzzle attachment for effects
examples.code:
local gun = workspace.Gun
local muzzle = Instance.new("Attachment")
muzzle.Name = "Muzzle"
muzzle.Position = Vector3.new(0, 0, -2)   -- tip of barrel, local space
muzzle.Parent = gun

local flash = Instance.new("ParticleEmitter")
flash.Rate = 0
flash.Parent = muzzle      -- emits from the attachment

local function fire()
    flash:Emit(5)
end
